messages:
Asha (support): Seeing a big spike of 504/502s from hosted inference in eu-west2 starting ~09:08 UTC. Customers reporting timeouts and auth retries. Gateway error rate >5% in az-b. sample req ids: abc123, def456

incidents-bot: incident created: SEV_P1 - regional networking (eu-west2)

Devon (oncall): Ack. Can you paste gateway logs + any pcap/traceroute you have? Is this limited to az-b or cross-AZ?

Asha (support): Uploading artifacts now -> s3://redwood-incidents/8073456789/pcap.tar.gz and logs at s3://.../gw-logs.gz. Initially looked like az-b but some retries show cross-AZ latency. Quick curl from our healthcheck: `curl -v https://gateway.eu-west2.redwood/v1/predict -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` returns `504 Gateway Timeout` at client side.

Marta (net-eng): I pulled the pcap. Seeing intermittent packet reordering and bursts of retransmits between our az-b egress and ProviderX backhaul (09:07:30 - 09:12:00). Also BGP withdraws for a handful of prefixes during that window. Traceroute snippet:
```
traceroute to transit-ix (192.0.2.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  203.0.113.5 (203.0.113.5)  4.6 ms  4.5 ms  4.4 ms
 3  * * *  (hairpin via provider backhaul)  120 ms  115 ms
 4  192.0.2.1 (192.0.2.1)  240 ms  238 ms  245 ms
```
Looks like a hairpin and path asymmetry on ProviderX.

Kai (ingress): Gateway metrics show queuing latencies spiking to 200-400ms and 1-2% packet loss for TCP flows out of az-b. Our retry middleware is hitting timeouts and producing upstream 502/504s; we also correlate 401s for some customers because the token refresh requests timed out and then retried after expiry.

Support Triage: We have 6 customers on CS calls, one escalated for SLA breach. They saw auth failures followed by billing noise (retries creating duplicate billable attempts). Need an ETA.

Devon (oncall): Immediate mitigation: shift traffic away from az-b. Marta/Kai - can we change routing weights to prefer az-c and fail open to eu-west1? Also disable aggressive client retries for gateway (set retries=0 -> increase timeouts) until network stabilizes.

Marta (net-eng): Coordinating with ProviderX right now. They acknowledge a misconfigured MPLS policy on their backhaul causing microloops and TTL decrement anomalies — looks like packets getting forwarded back to us (hairpin) and reordered. Provider says they'll push ACL/route fix; initial ETA ~18m. In the meantime I'm increasing preference for direct peering and advertising alternate paths.

DevOps: Applying immediate changes: `kubectl patch svc gateway -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Local"}}'` and updating Envoy timeout: `connect_timeout: 60s`, `retry_policy: none`. Rolling now.

Asha (support): After shifting ~60% traffic off az-b, error rate dropped from ~6.2% -> 1.1% over the last 5m. Customers reporting improved response. Still seeing a few 504s tied to old connections.

Devon (oncall): Good. Keep P1 until ProviderX confirms stable for 30m. Tasks: capture full BGP RIB/RIB changes, save pcaps, compile customer impact timeline, and escalate to provider ops if flap persists. I'll open the incident doc and add owners.

Support Triage: Noted for CS: proactive emails to affected customers and credit requests queued.

Marta (net-eng): ProviderX pushed fix at 09:30 UTC, BGP withdrawals stopped and packet reorder subsided. I'll keep monitoring for another 20m.

incidents-bot: incident severity -> P2 (mitigations applied) :thumbsup:

Devon (oncall): Postmortem checklist: capture provider comms, timeline, why our retry logic allowed token expiry to surface as 401s, and add a routing playbook to quickly shift weight between AZs. I'll assign follow-ups.

DevOps: Saved config diffs and the roll commands to the incident S3. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/8073456789

Asha (support): Customers on calls confirming stabilization. Marking affected CS cases for follow-up. Closing updates on this thread once provider confirms no recurrence. :white_check_mark:
